operations.exact_old_paragraph: 1.2 [Well-definedness and sesquilinearity] For fixed $(u_0,v_0)$ the map $(u,v)\mapsto\langle u,u_0\rangle_H\langle v,v_0\rangle_K$ is $\mathbb C$-linear on $H\times K$ (both factors are linear in their first argument by [F3]) and vanishes on each generating relation of $H_0$: for the additive relations by bilinearity of the pairings, and for $(ur,v)-(u,rv)$ because $\langle ur,u_0\rangle\langle v,v_0\rangle=\langle u,u_0\rangle\langle rv,v_0\rangle$ holds in the commutative field $\mathbb C$ with the $\mathbb C$-module structures. Hence it descends to a $\mathbb C$-linear functional of the first tensor argument, and the two-variable form descends in its first argument; interchanging the roles and using conjugate symmetry of both pairings gives that it also descends in the second argument and is conjugate-linear there. Finally $\langle z,w\rangle=\overline{\langle w,z\rangle}$ because both factor pairings have this property and complex conjugation is multiplicative. [given, F1, F3, algebra]
operations.exact_new_paragraph: 1.2 [Well-definedness and sesquilinearity] For fixed $(u_0,v_0)$, put $b_{u_0,v_0}(u,v)=\langle u,u_0\rangle_H\langle v,v_0\rangle_K$. By [F3] this is $\mathbb C$-bilinear in $u,v$, and $b_{u_0,v_0}(ur,v)=r b_{u_0,v_0}(u,v)=b_{u_0,v_0}(u,rv)$. Extend its values on the basis of $F=\mathbb Z^{(H\times K)}$ by $\widetilde b_{u_0,v_0}(\sum_i n_i e_{(u_i,v_i)})=\sum_i n_i b_{u_0,v_0}(u_i,v_i)$ for $n_i\in\mathbb Z$. This is a $\mathbb Z$-linear map on $F$, and additivity in each variable and the displayed balancing identity show that it vanishes on all three families of generators of $H_0$ in [F1], hence on $H_0$. It therefore induces an additive functional $\lambda_{u_0,v_0}:F/H_0\to\mathbb C$. Since $\widetilde b_{u_0,v_0}(L_c x)=c\widetilde b_{u_0,v_0}(x)$ for every $x\in F$, the scalar action of step 1.1 makes $\lambda_{u_0,v_0}$ complex-linear. For any finite representation $w=\sum_j u'_j\otimes v'_j$, the displayed form is consequently independent of the representation of its first argument $z$, being $\sum_j\lambda_{u'_j,v'_j}(z)$. On free representatives, conjugate symmetry of the factor pairings gives $\langle z,w\rangle=\overline{\langle w,z\rangle}$ term by term. Independence in the first argument applied to the right-hand side therefore gives independence of the representation of $w$ as well. The descended form is linear in $z$; conjugate symmetry then makes it conjugate-linear in $w$, and proves it is Hermitian. [given, F1, F3, step 1.1, algebra]
